"%1$s asked us to confirm it’s you. You’ll go straight back to them when you’re done."
"%1$s Your data is encrypted and used only for this check."
"To verify your identity, %1$s uses Identified to collect and check the information below."
", a short liveness check (turning your head)"
"Each document is captured in this flow and stored encrypted. We keep the image, the details read from it, and a record of when you submitted it."
"The details you enter — your name, date of birth and ID number — are compared against what your document says. A mismatch is flagged for a person to look at, not treated as fraud."
"Your proof of address needs to be a utility bill, bank statement or equivalent from the last 3 months showing your name and address."
"Your selfie and liveness images confirm that you are a real, live person and that your face matches the photo on your ID."
"The liveness check is a short movement prompt. It distinguishes a live person from a photo, a mask or a screen replay."

"Face match compares your selfie to the photo on your ID and produces a similarity score. It is not used to search for you in any other database, and we do not run face recognition against the public internet."
"Biometric data is treated as a special category of personal data everywhere we operate, which is why it is asked for separately here and processed only for this verification."
"We screen you against published sanctions and watchlists, verify any licence you hold with the authority that issued it, and carry out criminal-record screening."

"Sanctions screening matches your name and date of birth against the published OFAC, United Nations and European Union consolidated lists. A hit is a possible match, not a finding — a person reviews it before anything is reported."
"Licence verification checks the licence number and its status directly with the issuing authority."
"Criminal-record screening is carried out manually by a trained operator, who records the evidence behind the result so it can be explained or challenged later."
"Your proof of address establishes where you live, which is what makes a name match meaningful rather than a coincidence."
"Identity verification and background screening are decided separately. Your identity result is issued as soon as it is ready and is never reversed automatically by a later screening finding."
"A trained reviewer at Identified may look at what you submitted before a result is issued."
"Most cases are decided automatically. A case goes to a person when the automated checks disagree with each other, when an image is unclear, or when screening returns something that needs judgement."
"A reviewer sees your documents, your selfie and the check results. They do not see why you are being verified."
"An adverse screening finding always goes to a person. Nothing about your result changes on the strength of an unreviewed match."
"If a result was reached automatically, you can ask %1$s to have a person review it."
"Only to verify your identity%1$s for %2$s. The result of the check is shared with %3$s."
"%1$s receives the outcome, the reasons behind it, and the documents you submitted for this verification."

"Identified is a service of Fentord Technologies Limited, a company registered in Ghana. It runs the checks and stores the evidence on behalf of the business that sent you here, and does not use your data for its own purposes."
"We never sell your data and never use it for advertising or profiling."
"Your data is encrypted in transit and at rest, and processed under the data-protection law of the country you are verified in."

"Identified operates across Africa, so the law that applies is the one where you are — for example Ghana’s Data Protection Act 2012, Nigeria’s Data Protection Act 2023, Kenya’s Data Protection Act 2019 or South Africa’s POPIA — alongside the African Union’s Malabo Convention. The GDPR applies where you or your data are in the EU or UK."

"Those regimes agree on the part that matters here: background screening needs your consent, and that consent has to be evidenced. This screen is that evidence — your agreement is recorded against your session with a version and a timestamp, on our side rather than in your browser."

"Every connection uses TLS, and your documents and images are stored encrypted. What that does not mean is that nobody here can ever see them: deciding a case sometimes needs a person to look at a document, so access is restricted and logged rather than impossible. Anyone claiming end-to-end encryption for a check a human may review is overstating it."
"You can complain to the Data Protection Commission or equivalent supervisory authority in your country at any time."
"Your information is kept in line with %1$s’s policy and applicable law, then deleted."
"How long is set by %1$s, not by Identified. Ask %2$s how long they keep verification records."
"The evidence behind a decision is kept with the case for as long as the case is kept, so the result can be explained or challenged."
"Providing this data is voluntary, but verification can’t continue without it."
"You can ask %1$s for a copy of what was collected, ask for it to be corrected, or withdraw your consent."
"Withdrawing consent stops further processing. It does not undo a check that has already run, or a result already sent."
"Contact %1$s to exercise any of these. If you are not satisfied, you can go to your country’s data-protection authority."
"I have read and agree to the "
", and I consent to the collection and processing of my %1$s for verification."

"Identified (identified.cc) is a service of Fentord Technologies Limited, a company registered in Ghana. It provides identity verification and background screening, and these terms cover your use of this verification flow."

"%1$s asked you to verify. They decide what is checked, what the result is used for, and how long records are kept. Identified carries out the checks on their instructions and returns the result to them."
"This means there are two relationships: yours with Identified for the flow itself, and yours with the business that sent you, which is governed by their own terms. Nothing here replaces theirs."
"You must be old enough to give consent under the law of the country you are in, and you must be verifying yourself. Do not use this flow on behalf of another person."
"Submit documents that are genuine, current, and yours. Submit images of yourself, taken live, at the point you are asked for them."

"Do not attempt to defeat the checks — no photographs of photographs, masks, screen replays, edited images, or documents belonging to someone else. Doing so may be a criminal offence, and the attempt is recorded and reported to the business that sent you."
"3. What we check, and what we do not decide"

"Depending on what the business selected, we may check that your document is genuine and unexpired, that your face matches its photo, that you are physically present, and that you do not appear on published sanctions and watchlists. We may verify a licence with the authority that issued it, and carry out criminal-record screening."

"A check produces evidence, not a verdict about you. Sanctions screening in particular matches names and dates of birth, and people share both — a possible match is reviewed by a person before it is reported as anything."
"Identified does not decide whether you get the job, the account, or the ride. That decision belongs to the business that sent you, and any appeal against it goes to them."
"Most checks run automatically. A case is routed to a trained reviewer when the automated checks disagree, when an image cannot be read, or when screening returns something that needs judgement."
"Where a background screening finding is adverse, a person always decides what happens next. Nothing is reversed automatically on an unreviewed match."
"You can ask the business that sent you to have a person review any result reached about you."
"What we collect, why, and how long it is kept is set out on the Consent & privacy screen. Your agreement there is recorded with a version and a timestamp as evidence that it was given."

"Your biometric data is used to confirm you are live and that your face matches your document. It is not used to identify you anywhere else, and it is not sold, shared for advertising, or used to train anything."
"You can withdraw consent by contacting the business that sent you. Withdrawing stops further processing; it does not undo a check that has already run or a result already delivered."

"This flow is provided as-is. Verification links expire, cameras fail, and third-party authorities go offline; we do not promise the service will be uninterrupted or that a check will always complete."
"Nothing in these terms limits liability for fraud, for death or personal injury caused by negligence, or for anything else that cannot be limited under the law that applies to you."

"Fentord Technologies Limited is registered in Ghana, and these terms are governed by Ghanaian law. That choice does not take anything away from you: any consumer or data-protection right you hold under the law of your own country applies regardless of what these terms say, and cannot be signed away here."
"In particular, you keep the right to complain to the data-protection authority where you are — a Data Protection Commission or its equivalent — whatever these terms say."
"Terms in force for this session: version %1$s. If they change, the version recorded against your session stays the one you agreed to."

"Questions about the flow itself: hello@identified.cc (Fentord Technologies Limited, Ghana). Questions about why you were asked to verify, what the result was used for, or how long it is kept: the business that sent you."

"A photo of the front of your ID — the side with your photo."

"Fit all four edges inside the frame"

"Phone at eye level, about an arm’s length away."
